chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a one-eyed man who deliberately blinded the eye of a healthy person. He said: 'His eye is blinded.' I said: 'He becomes completely blind.' He said: 'It is the right (of the victim) which is blinded by him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of qisas for a one-eyed man who blinds a healthy person's eye?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of proportional retaliation (qisas) in Shi'a jurisprudence, specifically addressing the case of an 'awar (one-eyed) individual who deliberately blinds a healthy person. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the victim's right is satisfied by the loss of one eye, meaning the perpetrator is blinded in his remaining eye rather than being rendered completely blind, thereby avoiding excessive punishment. This ruling underscores the Shi'a scholarly emphasis on equity and the precise measurement of retribution in cases of bodily injury.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban, from a man,

(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a one-eyed man who blinded an eye of the healthy one deliberately. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His eye would be blinded’. I said, ‘He would become (completely) blind’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the right (of the victim) which would have been blinded by him’.
